campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 6, 2026
campbell.summary: The agenda for the October 6, 2026, Campbell City Council meeting listed three items: arranging temporary legal services while the city changes city attorneys, pay and working conditions for certain employee groups not covered by a union contract, and a market adjustment to the city manager's salary. The agenda describes items for the Council's consideration; it does not confirm what was discussed or decided.
keyTopics: The agenda listed temporary legal services to cover the city attorney transition
The agenda listed compensation and working conditions for unrepresented confidential, classified management, and unclassified management employees
The agenda listed a market adjustment to the city manager's salary

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 21, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the October 21, 2026, Saratoga City Council meeting listed routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and bill payments, along with final approval of two property splits and an annual update to the City Code. It also listed a proposal to start the process of creating a Climate Resilience District and a task force to support it.
keyTopics: Approval of the minutes from the September 30, 2026, special meeting and the October 7, 2026, council meeting
Acceptance of the city's vendor payment check registers dated 10/01/2026 and 10/08/2026
Final map approval to divide the property at 14860 Farwell Ave into two lots, and a separate item for the property at 18510 Sobey Rd
Annual 2026 City Code update, with a public hearing on changes to rules covering scheduling appeals and qualifications for City Commissioners
Resolutions to create a Climate Resilience District Task Force and to begin the process of establishing a Climate Resilience District

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 13, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the October 13, 2026, Los Altos City Council meeting listed a mix of routine financial and administrative items along with a few policy matters, including a home electrification rebate budget, updated below-market-rate housing guidelines, and a review of the handbook for city commissions and committees. It also listed an update on Ada's Cafe at the Community Center and the council's tentative calendar and Housing Element implementation schedule.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a resolution to move $78,000 from the general fund into the FY2026-27 budget for a residential electrification rebate program.
The agenda listed a resolution to approve Below Market Rate For-Sale and Rental Housing Guidelines, with a finding that the action is exempt from CEQA under Section 15061(b)(3).

The agenda listed two resolutions accepting completed public works: the FY 2025-2026 on-call sanitary sewer spot repairs and CCTV inspection services, and the FY 2024-2025 Annual Streets Project built by O'Grady Paving, Inc.
The agenda listed an updated Conflict of Interest Code for city staff and commissioners, tied to the Political Reform Act of 1974, for council approval.

The agenda listed a discussion of the Commission and Committee Handbook, an update on Ada's Cafe at the Community Center, and the tentative council calendar and Housing Element implementation schedule.

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 20, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, Los Gatos Town Council meeting listed routine business such as approving minutes from two October 6 meetings and receiving August financial and investment reports. It also listed several items authorizing the Town Manager to sign contracts or amendments, including one with Foster and Foster, a three-year agreement, and a lease amendment.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the October 6, 2026, Town Council Special Meeting and regular Town Council Meeting
Receipt of the August 2026 expenditure and revenue reports and the monthly financial and investment report
Approval and ratification of accounts payable check registers and the payroll report
Authorization for the Town Manager to execute a first amendment with Foster and Foster
Authorization for the Town Manager or designee to enter into a three-year agreement, and to negotiate and execute a lease amendment

san-jose.title: San José City Council — October 20, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, San José City Council meeting listed routine business such as approving minutes and special event sponsorships, along with several larger items. These included the City Manager's annual report, the Independent Police Auditor's year-end report, planning priorities, and three land-use matters involving specific properties.
keyTopics: The agenda listed the 2025-2026 City Manager's Annual Report and the 2025 Independent Police Auditor Year End Report.
Council was scheduled to consider Citywide Planning Work Plan Prioritization.
An appeal of the in-fill exemption for a data center use at 300 Holger Way was listed for an administrative hearing.

Items for 470 West San Carlos Street (environmental appeal and site development permit appeal) and 525 Race Street (early consideration of a privately initiated General Plan amendment) were on the agenda.

The agenda listed a conditional vacation of a portion of Spring Street between Asbury Street and West Taylor Street, plus special event approvals including a District 9 end-of-term farewell celebration and a Taiwan Retrocession Day proclamation and flag raising.

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — October 20, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council's agenda for October 20, 2026, listed a 6:30 p.m. study session focused on interviews with applicants for the Environmental Planning Commission. The rest of the published text covers public notices, including how to read meeting materials, request accessibility help, and submit comments to the Council.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a 6:30 p.m. study session for interviews of applicants to the Environmental Planning Commission.

Residents who want to comment can email city.council@mountainview.gov by 4:30 p.m. on the meeting date (with the agenda item number in the subject line) or fill out a blue speaker card to speak in person.

The public notice states there is a 90-day window to challenge certain City administrative decisions in Superior Court, and that court challenges to Council actions may be limited to issues raised at or before the public hearing.

Agenda materials are posted on the City's Legistar site and available at City Hall, the City Clerk's Office, and the Mountain View Library; accessibility help can be requested from the City Clerk 48 hours before the meeting.

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda for the October 6, 2026, Sunnyvale City Council meeting listed recognitions for the Little League Junior Division All-Stars and several observances, followed by routine business items and a few larger proposals. Items before the Council included a new ban on using drinking water to irrigate nonfunctional turf, a proposed ordinance on service worker retention, and public art for the Lakewood Park renovation.
keyTopics: Public hearing on an ordinance to implement state law AB 1572 by prohibiting the use of potable (drinking) water to irrigate nonfunctional turf, listed as exempt from CEQA under Guidelines Section 15307
Discussion and possible action to introduce a Service Worker Retention Ordinance
Approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation

Proposal to raise the not-to-exceed amount of the WSP USA Inc. environmental consulting agreement for the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill by $160,000 to $385,000 and extend it through October 17, 2028
Special recognitions for the 2026 Little League Junior Division All-Stars, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, and Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 20, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, Cupertino City Council meeting lists a regular session at 6:45 PM, preceded by a special meeting at 5:45 PM that includes a study session. The agenda lists three ceremonial recognitions, a consent calendar of routine items including a bridge design contract and a gymnastics program contract, two public hearings, and one action item about leasing a city-owned property.
keyTopics: The agenda lists a design contract of up to $1,278,700 with Biggs Cardoza Associates for the McClellan Road Bridge Project, plus acceptance of $850,000 in federal grant funds.

A public hearing is listed on amendments to the Health and Safety chapter of the Cupertino General Plan, along with updated appendices on community noise and geologic and seismic hazards and a new Health and Safety Background Report appendix.
A second public hearing is listed on financing approval for The RISE Block 5 Apartments Project, postponed from October 6, 2026.
The action calendar lists a proposed approach for leasing the city-owned commercial property at 22100 Stevens Creek Boulevard.

The consent calendar lists a gymnastics classes and camps contract with Bay Aerials Gymnastics of up to $480,000, extendable for two more years to a five-year total of $800,000, and an amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement.

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Neighborhood-University Relations Committee — October 19, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The agenda listed a special meeting of Santa Clara's Neighborhood University Relations Committee for October 19, 2026, at 6:00 pm in the City Hall Cafeteria, with the public able to attend in person or join remotely by Zoom or phone. The agenda listed a discussion of neighborhood nuisance issues in private rental leases, along with routine items and updates from city, university, and police staff.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a discussion of neighborhood nuisance topics in private property leases, plus possible direction to staff to return with ways to share the committee's input with property owners in the Old Quad neighborhood.
The agenda listed updates from the Community Development Department, Santa Clara University, and the Police Department.
The agenda listed approval of minutes from the committee's May 18, 2026, meeting and the committee's 2027 meeting calendar.
Residents could submit written comments to PlanningPublicComment@santaclaraca.gov by noon on the day of the meeting, naming the agenda item in the subject line; emails are not read aloud.

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — October 20, 2026
milpitas.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, Milpitas City Council meeting listed routine items like meeting calendars and minutes, along with a contract amendment for a new park design, a presentation from the county mosquito and vector control district, and a proposal to rename several community spaces. It also included the annual report and new work plans for the city's advisory commissions.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a proposed amendment to the design contract with Callander Associates Landscape Architecture for the Metro Tango Subdistrict Park, capped at $130,000.
The agenda listed a presentation from the Santa Clara County Mosquito and Vector Control District.

The agenda listed a resolution to rename the Cesar Chavez Community Garden as the "Milpitas Community Garden" and Cesar Chavez Plaza as "Milpitas Civic Center Plaza," and to name the garden in Delano Manongs Park the "Larry Itliong Community Garden."

The agenda listed acceptance of the FY2025-26 annual report from the city's commissions and approval of FY2026-27 work plans for eight commissions, including the Arts Commission, Economic Development and Trade Commission, Library and Education Advisory Commission, and Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources Commission.

The agenda listed routine items: the October and November 2026 meeting calendar, minutes from the October 6, 2026, meeting, a preview of items expected at the next regular meeting, and the list of items requested by Councilmembers.

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — October 15, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda for Palo Alto's Architectural Review Board meeting on October 15, 2026, listed a public hearing on a request from AT&T to add new wireless equipment to two existing city-owned wooden utility poles in the public right-of-way, near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue. The agenda describes the project as exempt from California's environmental review law because it involves existing facilities.
keyTopics: Public hearing on AT&T's request to add new antennas, remote radio units, and associated equipment to two existing city-owned wood utility poles near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue
Proposal includes seven-foot fiberglass pole extensions on the poles; the two sites are classified as Tier 2 general wireless communication facilities
Item is listed as quasi-judicial (file number 26PLN-00229), with a supplemental report added to the agenda
Agenda lists the project as exempt from environmental review under CEQA Guideline Section 15301 (Existing Facilities); the poles are in the public right-of-way, so no zoning district applies
